project.name: GLib
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable checkout available in `gt_results/arvo_42506130/_work/src/glib` resolves local Git HEAD to `42a5f1d387e148b2e94d9fe3a5a3826305e56aac`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `5cdacced3fe58965d1ff592bd8fc3c100accede4`. This trace is grounded in that staged source, whose line map matches the saved ASan crash at `gio/gthreadedresolver.c:699`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42506130 (glib): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 12 found by fuzz target fuzz_resolver [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42506130
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged source checkout is `42a5f1d387e148b2e94d9fe3a5a3826305e56aac`, while sample metadata names `5cdacced3fe58965d1ff592bd8fc3c100accede4`; the saved ASan line map and the staged patch both ground the vulnerable path in `gio/gthreadedresolver.c`. The staged witness is the single byte `0x20`, so `test_for_rrtype()` passes `g_resolver_records_from_res_query()` a one-byte heap buffer with `len == 1`. Inside that function the only length check rejects `len <= 0`, so the undersized reply is admitted without the patch's missing `len_unsigned < sizeof (HEADER)` guard. The vulnerable code then aliases the one-byte buffer as `HEADER *` and immediately reads `header->qdcount` as though a full DNS header were present. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 12` at `gio/gthreadedresolver.c:699`, and the report says the accessed address is 10 bytes to the right of the 1-byte fuzz-input region. The patch fixes this exact obligation by rejecting replies shorter than `sizeof (HEADER)` before any header access.

source.description: First project statement on the vulnerable path that consumes the attacker-controlled reply length and decides whether DNS parsing continues.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_42506130/poc` is the exact one-byte file `0x20` (sha256 `36a9e7f1c95b82ffb99743e0c5c4ce95d83c9a430aac59f84ef3cbfab6145068`). `test_for_rrtype()` passes that byte unchanged as `answer` with `len == 1` into `g_resolver_records_from_res_query()` after only the harness-side `data_len > G_MAXSSIZE` check.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Incomplete length validation. The function rejects only nonpositive replies, so a positive reply shorter than a DNS `HEADER` still reaches header parsing. The patch adds the missing `len_unsigned < sizeof (HEADER)` rejection immediately after this block.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The parser reads the DNS question-count field through the `HEADER` alias even though the saved witness buffer is only one byte long.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 12` at `gio/gthreadedresolver.c:699:11` and says the faulting address is 10 bytes to the right of the 1-byte fuzz-input region.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant attacker state is the exact positive but too-short length `len == 1`. That one-byte extent is what bypasses the only existing guard and makes every later header access out-of-bounds.

parser_admitted.code:
record_list = g_resolver_records_from_res_query ("rrname",
                                                   rrtype,
                                                   data,
                                                   data_len,
                                                   0,
                                                   NULL);
parser_admitted.description: The OSS-Fuzz shim forwards the raw fuzz buffer and its exact length straight into `g_resolver_records_from_res_query()` after only the harness-side `data_len > G_MAXSSIZE` check. The crash happens before `rrtype` influences control flow.

fine_trace.note: Source and root cause. The staged witness reaches this function as a one-byte heap buffer, so `len == 1`. This block rejects only `len <= 0`, leaving the undersized reply on the vulnerable path; there is no `len_unsigned < sizeof (HEADER)` rejection before DNS-header parsing begins.
The parser aliases the same one-byte fuzz buffer as a `HEADER *`. From this point, field accesses through `header` assume the reply already contains the fixed DNS header layout.

Sink. The first DNS-header field read dereferences the `HEADER` alias from step 2 even though step 1 admitted only a one-byte reply. The saved ASan run reports this line as `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 12`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch casts `len` to `gsize` and adds `if (len_unsigned < sizeof (HEADER)) return NULL` before any `HEADER` aliasing or field reads, which directly blocks the one-byte witness. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, so this is a source-level conclusion from the diff rather than fixed-runtime evidence.

poc.trigger: The staged witness `poc` is the one-byte file `0x20` (sha256 `36a9e7f1c95b82ffb99743e0c5c4ce95d83c9a430aac59f84ef3cbfab6145068`). `test_for_rrtype()` forwards it unchanged as `answer,len == 1` to `g_resolver_records_from_res_query()`, the function rejects only `len <= 0`, and the next header read `header->qdcount` triggers the saved ASan `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 12` at `gio/gthreadedresolver.c:699`.

format.name: 1-byte raw resolver answer
format.contract: A one-byte buffer supplied to `fuzz_resolver` is sufficient for this path, because the crash occurs before any content-dependent parsing and depends only on `len == 1` surviving the existing `len <= 0` guard. The verified witness is the exact staged byte `0x20`.
